synergy_categories_9.evidence: Combined 49+15=64 tools. Hermes provides voice/image/MoA/skills, CC provides code-aware Read/Edit/Grep/Glob + extended thinking. Zero duplication in core tools.
synergy_categories_9.roi: Immediate — combined tool surface exceeds any single agent

synergy_categories_9.evidence: Natural pipeline: Hermes receives task via Telegram → delegates coding to CC → CC returns result → Hermes persists as skill + sends result back to user. Output→input chain is clean.
synergy_categories_9.roi: High — unlocks non-developer access to CC coding power

synergy_categories_9.evidence: Hermes provides 15 platform adapters (access layer), CC provides IDE integration + 200K context (depth layer). Together: accessible from anywhere AND deep when needed.
synergy_categories_9.roi: High — solves CC's biggest gap (platform reach) and Hermes's biggest gap (coding depth)

synergy_categories_9.evidence: Hermes has session FTS5 search + auto skill creation. CC has CLAUDE.md + auto-memory + rules. Combined: Hermes learns from CC coding sessions, CC benefits from Hermes's cross-session recall. Mastery analysis confirms CC loses ~50% artifacts — Hermes persistence layer fixes this.
Hermes routes simple tasks to cheap models (Haiku, DeepSeek), reserves CC Opus for complex coding. Estimated 40-60% token cost reduction for mixed workloads.
Hermes SQLite sessions + CC CLAUDE.md memory. Shared context about user preferences, project state, and past decisions. Hermes USER.md feeds CC auto-memory and vice versa.
CC permission sandboxing (5 modes) + Hermes approval flows + Tirith security + skills_guard. Combined posture stronger but requires reconciling two different security models.
synergy_categories_9.roi: Low — security models are architecturally different

synergy_categories_9.evidence: Hermes (open source, community-driven) + CC (enterprise, Anthropic-backed). Positioning as 'best of both worlds' is compelling but requires careful messaging.
Both support MCP protocol. Hermes skills could be exposed as MCP tools to CC. CC hooks could trigger Hermes actions. Shared MCP bridge is the natural integration point.
synergy_categories_9.roi: High — MCP is the common protocol

integration_patterns.name: Gateway Delegation
integration_patterns.description: Hermes receives requests from any platform, classifies intent, delegates coding tasks to CC via `claude -p`, returns results to user
pros: Each tool does what it's best at
No modification needed to either tool

integration_patterns.name: MCP Tool Bridge
integration_patterns.description: Hermes exposes its unique tools (voice, image gen, session search, skills) as MCP server. CC calls them as needed
integration_patterns.when_to_use: When working inside CC but needing Hermes capabilities

integration_patterns.name: Skill Pipeline
integration_patterns.description: CC solves coding task → Hermes skill_manager extracts solution as SKILL.md → syncs to CC .claude/skills/ → next session CC has the skill

integration_patterns.name: MoA Coding Consensus
integration_patterns.description: Hermes MoA tool sends coding problem to CC (Opus) + Gemini + GPT-5 + DeepSeek, aggregates best solution
integration_patterns.when_to_use: Critical coding decisions, architecture reviews, complex debugging

integration_patterns.name: Session Recall Augmentation
integration_patterns.description: CC hooks into Hermes session search before starting work: 'What have I done before on this codebase?' Hermes FTS5 provides context from past sessions
integration_patterns.when_to_use: Resuming work on a codebase after days/weeks

friction_points.mitigation: MCP + CLI bridge — no shared runtime needed

friction_points.description: Different auth models (OpenRouter API keys vs Anthropic API)
friction_points.mitigation: Each manages own auth. No shared credentials needed
Memory sync at session boundary via file export/import

friction_points.description: Different security models (approval flow vs permission modes)
friction_points.mitigation: Accept both models coexist. Hermes gates platform access, CC gates code execution
Hermes handles context compression; CC operates in its native 200K window

friction_points.description: Deployment model mismatch (VPS daemon vs local CLI)
friction_points.mitigation: Hermes runs on VPS as daemon; CC runs locally or cloud-scheduled. Communicate via MCP/CLI
No licensing conflict — Hermes is MIT, CC is pay-per-use. Integration is just API/CLI calls

value_equation.interpretation: Combined value 20.5% higher than best standalone (Hermes 68.1). Integration cost moderate, friction low. Strong positive ROI.
